traveller: Marco Polo: Venetian man with warm light-olive skin, dark brown wavy hair, long straight nose and dark brows. At departure age17: slim, clean-shaven, simple brown wool tunic and muted rust cloak. During eastern travel age18–24: lean build and short dark beard emerging. In China age25–36: short dark beard, plain practical belted Yuan-period travel robe in muted brown or blue-grey, no royal insignia. At sea and home age37–44: weathered face, dark beard beginning to grey, practical travel clothes. Father Niccolo and uncle Maffeo are distinctly older bearded merchants, never Marco duplicates. Clothing adapts to climate. No European Renaissance hats or Qing queues.

scenes.title: Leaving Venice
scenes.caption: In 1271, seventeen-year-old Marco left Venice with his father Niccolò and his uncle Maffeo. The brothers had already been to Kublai Khan's court, and were going back with his request for a hundred learned Christians and oil from Jerusalem.

scenes.title: Across the Adriatic

scenes.title: The harbour at Acre
scenes.caption: Acre was the last great crusader port in the Holy Land, and the papal legate Teobaldo Visconti was there. The Polos went to him first, to ask leave to fetch the oil from Jerusalem.

scenes.title: From the port to the road
scenes.caption: At Ayas, news reached them that the legate had been elected Pope Gregory X. He called them back to Acre and sent two Dominican friars with them, but at Ayas the friars heard that the Mamluks had invaded Armenia, and turned back.

scenes.title: Carpets of Turcomania

scenes.title: The tombs shown at Saveh
scenes.caption: At Saba, now Saveh, he was shown three handsome tombs said to hold the three Magi, their bodies still whole. He was told the three kings had set out from here to worship the newborn Christ.

scenes.caption: Near Camadi, raiders he called Caraonas fell on the caravan, under cover of a darkness he believed they raised by magic. The Polos escaped to a village called Conosalmi; most of their companions were killed or sold as slaves.

scenes.title: Old Hormuz on the mainland

scenes.caption: He distrusted the local ships: their planks were sewn together with twine made from coconut husk, without iron nails, and many were lost at sea. The Polos chose not to sail for China from here.

scenes.title: The summer capital
scenes.caption: In 1275 the Polos reached Kublai at Shangdu, his summer capital, more than three years after leaving Venice. The Khan had sent riders forty days' journey out to meet them.
scenes.prompt: Wide approach from grassy plain toward Yuan Shangdu low perimeter walls and modest roofed palace complex, small mounted group with Marco age21, no Forbidden City or gigantic white European marble castle.

composition.view: Wide approach from grassy plain toward Yuan Shangdu low perimeter walls and modest roofed palace complex, small mounted group with Marco age21, no Forbidden City or gigantic white European marble castle.

evidence.passage: Prologue: arrival at the court; Book I: Chandu.

scenes.title: The palace of cane
scenes.caption: Inside Shangdu's park stood a palace of cane, gilded and lacquered, that could be taken apart and moved. He wrote that more than two hundred silk cords held it up against the wind.
scenes.prompt: Close oblique structural study modest elegant Yuan cane pavilion corner, lacquered timber posts supporting split bamboo roof tiles, taut guy ropes tied to stakes, coherent load-bearing frame, no fantasy all-stone palace.

composition.view: Close oblique structural study modest elegant Yuan cane pavilion corner, lacquered timber posts supporting split bamboo roof tiles, taut guy ropes tied to stakes, coherent load-bearing frame, no fantasy all-stone palace.

evidence.passage: Book I: Chandu, the cane palace.

scenes.title: An audience with Kublai
scenes.caption: The Polos knelt before Kublai and gave him the Pope's letters and the oil from Jerusalem, and Niccolò presented his son. The Khan welcomed Marco and took him into his household.
scenes.prompt: Interior from behind three modest Venetian visitors facing mature Kublai seated on low raised cushion dais in Yuan hall, Marco21 at side listening, Mongol robe and simple cap, respectful distant faces, no Qing throne or European crown.

composition.view: Interior from behind three modest Venetian visitors facing mature Kublai seated on low raised cushion dais in Yuan hall, Marco21 at side listening, Mongol robe and simple cap, respectful distant faces, no Qing throne or European crown.

evidence.passage: Prologue: the audience with Kublai.

scenes.title: Streets of the new capital
scenes.caption: Kublai's new capital, Dadu, which Polo called Khanbaliq, was laid out on a grid, its streets so straight that one could see from gate to gate. He wrote that the whole city was planned like a chessboard.
scenes.prompt: Wide oblique Yuan Dadu street with broad earthen road, low tiled timber shopfronts and carts, distant palace wall, no Ming Forbidden City towers or Qing queues or modern paving.

composition.view: Wide oblique Yuan Dadu street with broad earthen road, low tiled timber shopfronts and carts, distant palace wall, no Ming Forbidden City towers or Qing queues or modern paving.

evidence.passage: Book II: the city of Taidu.

scenes.title: Paper accepted as money
scenes.caption: He was amazed that the Khan's subjects accepted paper money, made from mulberry bark and stamped with the Khan's red seal. Anyone who forged it, he wrote, was put to death.
scenes.prompt: Close desk-level Yuan paper money preparation, official hand presses square red seal onto fibrous rectangular note lying FLAT on table, other indistinct black printed notes nearby, no readable invented characters or modern banknotes.

composition.view: Close desk-level Yuan paper money preparation, official hand presses square red seal onto fibrous rectangular note lying FLAT on table, other indistinct black printed notes nearby, no readable invented characters or modern banknotes.

evidence.passage: Book II: how the Khan makes paper pass for money.

scenes.title: Fresh horses at a post station
scenes.caption: He described the Khan's post roads, with stations every twenty-five or thirty miles keeping hundreds of horses ready. Riders changing horses at each station could carry a message more than two hundred miles in a day.
scenes.prompt: Courtyard side view Marco late20s in plain travel coat watching official courier exchange horses, groom holds fresh horse reins, low Yuan post station, coherent saddles and separate reins, no modern mailbags.

composition.view: Courtyard side view Marco late20s in plain travel coat watching official courier exchange horses, groom holds fresh horse reins, low Yuan post station, coherent saddles and separate reins, no modern mailbags.

evidence.passage: Book II: the Khan's posts and runners.

scenes.title: The bridge and its stone lions
scenes.caption: Ten miles from the capital he crossed a marble bridge over a river he called Pulisanghin, Persian for 'stone bridge', with carved lions along its parapets. He counted twenty-four arches; the Lugou Bridge has eleven, and English speakers still call it the Marco Polo Bridge.
scenes.prompt: Low eye-level along Lugou Bridge stone balustrade with small carved guardian lions on posts, roadway securely supported and visible repeating low arches only to side, Yuan era no modern traffic, do not draw24arches.

composition.view: Low eye-level along Lugou Bridge stone balustrade with small carved guardian lions on posts, roadway securely supported and visible repeating low arches only to side, Yuan era no modern traffic, do not draw24arches.

evidence.passage: Book II: the river Pulisanghin and its bridge.

scenes.title: Where the roads divide
scenes.caption: A little beyond the bridge was Juju, now Zhuozhou, where, he wrote, the roads parted. One ran west through Cathay toward Tibet and Yunnan; the other ran south-east to Manzi, the former Song lands.
scenes.prompt: Over-shoulder view Marco around28 and mounted guide at unmarked fork of two earthen roads outside low town gate, one western track hills and one southeast canal plain, no written signposts or modern map.

composition.view: Over-shoulder view Marco around28 and mounted guide at unmarked fork of two earthen roads outside low town gate, one western track hills and one southeast canal plain, no written signposts or modern map.

evidence.passage: Book II: Juju and the parting of the roads.

scenes.title: Silk in Hejian
scenes.caption: Going south toward Manzi, he passed Cacanfu, now Hejian, a city that made silk and cloth of silk and gold. He noted a church of Nestorian Christians there.
scenes.prompt: Interior side view Yuan-era silk reeling worker with small wooden reel and warm shallow basin of cocoons, thread continuous and plausible, timber window light, no industrial spinning machinery.

composition.view: Interior side view Yuan-era silk reeling worker with small wooden reel and warm shallow basin of cocoons, thread continuous and plausible, timber window light, no industrial spinning machinery.

evidence.passage: Book II: Cacanfu.

scenes.title: Drawing salt from the earth
scenes.caption: At Cianglu, now Changlu, he watched salt made from the earth: people heaped up salty soil, poured water over it, and collected the brine that drained out. The Changlu salt works remained among China's largest for centuries.
scenes.prompt: Medium side view simple earthen salt leaching installation, salty soil in raised shallow wooden trough, brine drains into ceramic vessel beneath, worker carries bucket, no modern pipes or chemical plant.

composition.view: Medium side view simple earthen salt leaching installation, salty soil in raised shallow wooden trough, brine drains into ceramic vessel beneath, worker carries bucket, no modern pipes or chemical plant.

evidence.passage: Book II: Cianglu, salt-making; the later salt works are contextual.

scenes.title: Crystals in the salt pan
scenes.caption: The brine was then boiled in great iron pans until the salt crystallised, white and fine. He noted that the trade brought the Khan a large revenue.
scenes.prompt: Close low view shallow rectangular iron evaporation pan above brick hearth, thin steam, salt crystals gathered at one edge with wooden rake, coherent level liquid surface, no giant bubbling cauldron.

composition.view: Close low view shallow rectangular iron evaporation pan above brick hearth, thin steam, salt crystals gathered at one edge with wooden rake, coherent level liquid surface, no giant bubbling cauldron.

evidence.passage: Book II: Cianglu.

scenes.title: A waterway joining north and south
scenes.caption: At Sinjumatu, now Jining, he saw a river divided in two, one half flowing north toward Cathay and the other south toward Manzi. This was the summit of the Grand Canal, where Kublai's engineers were cutting new channels to carry grain to the capital.
scenes.prompt: Elevated riverbank sketch canal junction near Yuan Jining, small flat-bottom cargo boats and workers repairing earth embankment, modest engineering, no modern concrete locks or claim allmodernGrandCanalcomplete1282.

composition.view: Elevated riverbank sketch canal junction near Yuan Jining, small flat-bottom cargo boats and workers repairing earth embankment, modest engineering, no modern concrete locks or claim allmodernGrandCanalcomplete1282.

scenes.title: Crossing into Manzi
scenes.caption: He crossed the Caramoran, the Mongols' 'Black River', as he called the Yellow River, which then reached the sea by way of the Huai. On the far bank lay Coiganju, now Huai'an, the gateway to Manzi.
scenes.prompt: View from broad wooden ferry deck Marco and local passengers beside secured pack bundles, yellow-brown river and low far bank, ferry fully buoyant with plausible low gunwale, no standing people outside hull.

composition.view: View from broad wooden ferry deck Marco and local passengers beside secured pack bundles, yellow-brown river and low far bank, ferry fully buoyant with plausible low gunwale, no standing people outside hull.

evidence.passage: Book II: the Caramoran and Coiganju.

scenes.title: Fish beside the canal
scenes.caption: At Cayu, now Gaoyou, the road ran along a stone causeway beside the canal, through wide water and marsh. He noted fish and game in great abundance.
scenes.prompt: Ground-level riverside study woven baskets of fresh modest carp and net drying on wooden poles, canal boat beyond, Yuan fishermen small background, no modern metal fish market counters.

composition.view: Ground-level riverside study woven baskets of fresh modest carp and net drying on wooden poles, canal boat beyond, Yuan fishermen small background, no modern metal fish market counters.

evidence.passage: Book II: Cayu.

scenes.title: Merchants at Yangzhou
scenes.caption: Yangiu, now Yangzhou, was a great city ruling twenty-seven others, and he claimed to have governed it for three years on the Khan's orders. No Chinese record mentions him, and many scholars think he held a lesser post, perhaps in the salt administration.
scenes.prompt: Wide oblique busy Yuan Yangzhou canal quay, low warehouses and bales unloaded via gangplank, merchants ordinary scale, no Marco on governor throne or Qing scenic garden.

composition.view: Wide oblique busy Yuan Yangzhou canal quay, low warehouses and bales unloaded via gangplank, merchants ordinary scale, no Marco on governor throne or Qing scenic garden.

evidence.passage: Book II: Yanju; Pelliot and Haw on the governorship claim.

scenes.title: A Christian church at Zhenjiang
scenes.caption: At Chinghianfu, now Zhenjiang, he found two Nestorian churches built in 1278 by Mar Sargis, a Christian whom the Khan had made governor. A Chinese gazetteer of about 1333 confirms him, and credits him with seven churches, six of them around the city.
scenes.prompt: Quiet Yuan Jiangnan courtyard with modest timber-roofed East Syriac Christian meeting hall and plain cross over door, local adult worshippers, no Gothic cathedral or invented exact monumental facade.

composition.view: Quiet Yuan Jiangnan courtyard with modest timber-roofed East Syriac Christian meeting hall and plain cross over door, local adult worshippers, no Gothic cathedral or invented exact monumental facade.

evidence.passage: Book II: Chinghianfu; Zhishun Zhenjiang zhi on Mar Sargis.

scenes.title: A bridge in Suzhou
scenes.caption: He described Suju, now Suzhou, as a very great city with six thousand stone bridges, high enough for a galley to pass under. Its people lived by trade and crafts.
scenes.prompt: Water-level view under edge of small stone arch bridge toward Yuan Suzhou canal houses, plain white plaster and dark tile, coherent arch springing on two banks, no modern tourism lantern rows.

composition.view: Water-level view under edge of small stone arch bridge toward Yuan Suzhou canal houses, plain white plaster and dark tile, coherent arch springing on two banks, no modern tourism lantern rows.

evidence.passage: Book II: Suju.

scenes.title: Choosing a length of silk
scenes.caption: So much silk was made around Suzhou, he wrote, that everyone was dressed in it, and great quantities went to market. He noted that its merchants were rich, but not men of war.
scenes.prompt: Side view Marco early30s feeling edge of folded silk while Chinese merchant unrolls fabric over counter, hands simple and separated, Yuan robes and caps, no Qing queues or modern measuring tape.

composition.view: Side view Marco early30s feeling edge of folded silk while Chinese merchant unrolls fabric over counter, hands simple and separated, Yuan robes and caps, no Qing queues or modern measuring tape.

evidence.passage: Book II: Suju.

scenes.title: Waterways of Hangzhou
scenes.caption: He called Quinsay, now Hangzhou, 'beyond dispute the finest and noblest city in the world'. Its name came from xingzai, the 'temporary capital' of the fallen Song, and he counted twelve thousand bridges over its canals.
scenes.prompt: Wide elevated oblique late13c Hangzhou urban canal with several modest stone bridges at believable intervals, dense low tiled roofs and cargo boats, no thousands of literal bridges or modern WestLake skyline.

composition.view: Wide elevated oblique late13c Hangzhou urban canal with several modest stone bridges at believable intervals, dense low tiled roofs and cargo boats, no thousands of literal bridges or modern WestLake skyline.

scenes.title: A southern market
scenes.caption: He described ten great market squares in Quinsay, each holding a market three days a week for forty or fifty thousand people. He listed fish brought fresh from the sea every day, game, and pears weighing ten pounds each.
scenes.prompt: Eye-level sheltered market lane, fish basket stall foreground, vegetables and ceramic bowls farther back, Yuan civilian shoppers in varied side/rear poses, no uniform exotic costumes or presentdayshop signs.

composition.view: Eye-level sheltered market lane, fish basket stall foreground, vegetables and ceramic bowls farther back, Yuan civilian shoppers in varied side/rear poses, no uniform exotic costumes or presentdayshop signs.

evidence.passage: Book II: Kinsay, its markets.

scenes.title: Boats on the lake
scenes.caption: On West Lake, he wrote, pleasure boats with tables and painted cabins carried parties of friends, who could see the whole city and its palaces from the water. Fine houses and Buddhist monasteries stood all around the shore.
scenes.prompt: View from under simple covered pleasure boat awning across West Lake, Marco early30s seated side silhouette with local companions, distant low shore pavilions and wooded hills, no modern skyscrapers or Qianlong-era marble boat.

composition.view: View from under simple covered pleasure boat awning across West Lake, Marco early30s seated side silhouette with local companions, distant low shore pavilions and wooded hills, no modern skyscrapers or Qianlong-era marble boat.

scenes.title: Toward the Fujian hills
scenes.caption: From Quinsay the road south ran up into hill country, through towns he called Vuju and Ghiuju, now Wuzhou and Quzhou. He noted prosperous towns, plenty of silk, and canes of great size along the way.
scenes.prompt: Wide low view winding foot-and-packhorse trail among wooded southern Chinese hills, creek and small timber wayside shelter, tiny travellers, no modern terraced tea tourist road or hugeMingbridge.

composition.view: Wide low view winding foot-and-packhorse trail among wooded southern Chinese hills, creek and small timber wayside shelter, tiny travellers, no modern terraced tea tourist road or hugeMingbridge.

evidence.passage: Book II: Vuju, Ghiuju and the road to Fuju.

scenes.title: The chickens with soft plumage
scenes.caption: At Quenlinfu, now Jian'ou, he noted handsome stone bridges, ginger and galingale. He also described hens with no feathers, only a coat like a cat's fur: the breed now called the silkie.
scenes.prompt: Close natural-history sketch two silkie chickens with soft fluffy white and grey plumage, small dark beaks and normal chicken legs standing in earth courtyard, ginger roots in basket side, no mammal fur anatomy.

evidence.passage: Book II: Quenlinfu.

scenes.title: Sugar for trade
scenes.caption: He described Fuju, now Fuzhou, as a great trading city, where ships brought pearls and precious stones from India, and sugar was made in enormous quantities. Nearby, he said, men from 'Babylon', meaning Egypt, had taught the people to refine it.
scenes.prompt: Close workshop view sugarcane stalks, thick syrup in shallow pot and simple unglazed conical draining molds upright on stand, wooden tools, Yuan Fujian setting, no modern white sugar cubes or factory centrifuge.

composition.view: Close workshop view sugarcane stalks, thick syrup in shallow pot and simple unglazed conical draining molds upright on stand, wooden tools, Yuan Fujian setting, no modern white sugar cubes or factory centrifuge.

evidence.passage: Book II: Fuju and Unken.

scenes.title: The port of Zaiton
scenes.caption: He called Zaiton, now Quanzhou, one of the two greatest ports in the world. For every shipload of pepper that went to Alexandria for Christendom, he wrote, a hundred came to Zaiton.
scenes.prompt: Broad shore view Yuan Quanzhou estuary harbor, wooden seagoing Chinese junks with plausible battened sails and separate smaller craft, tiled warehouses and low pagoda inland, no Qing warjunk or gigantic Ming treasure ship.

composition.view: Broad shore view Yuan Quanzhou estuary harbor, wooden seagoing Chinese junks with plausible battened sails and separate smaller craft, tiled warehouses and low pagoda inland, no Qing warjunk or gigantic Ming treasure ship.

evidence.passage: Book II: Zaiton.

scenes.title: Loading for the voyage
scenes.caption: Kublai fitted out fourteen four-masted ships for the princess's voyage, some with crews of two hundred and fifty. He had them provisioned, Polo wrote, for two years at sea.
scenes.prompt: Low dock-level view stevedores roll tied ceramic storage jar carefully onto sturdy gangplank leading to ship opening, bundled cargo securely in hold, no impossible floating loads or modern pallet.

composition.view: Low dock-level view stevedores roll tied ceramic storage jar carefully onto sturdy gangplank leading to ship opening, bundled cargo securely in hold, no impossible floating loads or modern pallet.

scenes.title: The princess's escort
scenes.caption: In 1291 the Polos sailed with Kököchin, a seventeen-year-old Mongol princess sent as a bride to the Ilkhan Arghun. A Yuan post-station record of 1290, found by Yang Zhijiu in 1941, names her three Persian envoys exactly as Polo does: Uladai, Abishqa and Khoja.
scenes.prompt: Medium side deck view adult Mongol princess in modest Yuan silk robe and soft court cap seated under awning with attendants, Marco late30s consulting two Persian envoys at respectful distance, no romantic scene or Qingheaddress.

composition.view: Medium side deck view adult Mongol princess in modest Yuan silk robe and soft court cap seated under awning with attendants, Marco late30s consulting two Persian envoys at respectful distance, no romantic scene or Qingheaddress.

evidence.passage: Prologue: Cocachin and the envoys Oulatai, Apusca and Coja; Yang Zhijiu (1941).

scenes.title: Along the coast of Champa
scenes.caption: The fleet coasted south to Ciamba, the kingdom of Champa, which Marco had visited in 1285. Its king paid the Khan tribute in elephants and aloes-wood, and had, he said, 326 children.
scenes.prompt: From ship offshore toward forested centralVietnam coast, small river mouth and low Cham brick temple tower inland, local fishing boats, no Angkor Wat skyline transplanted to beach.

composition.view: From ship offshore toward forested centralVietnam coast, small river mouth and low Cham brick temple tower inland, local fishing boats, no Angkor Wat skyline transplanted to beach.

scenes.title: Sondur and Condur
scenes.caption: Past Champa, he noted two islands he called Sondur and Condur, now the Côn Sơn islands. Later sailors knew them as Pulo Condore, a landmark on the route between China and the Malay world.
scenes.prompt: Very wide sea-level rocky wooded Con Son island profile, open blue-grey sea and cloud shadows, only small corner of ship rail foreground, no modern prison buildings or generic tropicalresort.

composition.view: Very wide sea-level rocky wooded Con Son island profile, open blue-grey sea and cloud shadows, only small corner of ship rail foreground, no modern prison buildings or generic tropicalresort.

scenes.title: Feeling a way through the shallows
scenes.caption: Near Pentam, now Bintan, he wrote, the sea between the islands was so shallow, only four paces deep, that ships had to draw up their rudders. Beyond lay the strait leading to Sumatra.
scenes.prompt: Close view from stern quarter Chinese seagoing junk, crew work wooden lifting tackle to raise large vertical stern rudder in shallow pale water, clearly connected ropes and blade, distant mangrove coast; no detached modern propeller.

composition.view: Close view from stern quarter Chinese seagoing junk, crew work wooden lifting tackle to raise large vertical stern rudder in shallow pale water, clearly connected ropes and blade, distant mangrove coast; no detached modern propeller.

scenes.title: Waiting for the monsoon
scenes.caption: The fleet waited five months at Samara, on Sumatra, for the monsoon to turn. The party built a timber stockade against the man-eaters they had heard lived inland, and traded with the islanders for food.
scenes.prompt: Medium view Marco late30s mends travel bag under simple palm-thatch shelter, rain outside and anchored ships distant, mixed local and visiting sailors naturally at work, no threatening stereotypes.

composition.view: Medium view Marco late30s mends travel bag under simple palm-thatch shelter, rain outside and anchored ships distant, mixed local and visiting sailors naturally at work, no threatening stereotypes.

scenes.title: The anchorage in rain
scenes.caption: He called Sumatra 'Java the Less', and noted that from here the Pole Star could no longer be seen. He described the palm wine drawn from cut branches, and the sago flour of the neighbouring kingdom of Fansur.
scenes.prompt: Shore-level sheltered view tropical rain curtains over northern Sumatra anchorage, ships silhouettes beyond wet palm leaves, woven baskets raised on timber supports foreground, no shipbuilding lesson or giant waves inside calm bay.

composition.view: Shore-level sheltered view tropical rain curtains over northern Sumatra anchorage, ships silhouettes beyond wet palm leaves, woven baskets raised on timber supports foreground, no shipbuilding lesson or giant waves inside calm bay.

scenes.title: Coconuts on an island shore
scenes.caption: Sailing north-west, they passed Necuveram, the Nicobar Islands, where he said people went naked and had no king. He listed red sandalwood, coconuts and brazilwood among its trees.
scenes.prompt: Close botanical shoreline sketch split and whole mature coconuts beneath palm frond, fibrous husks and rounded stones, clear shallows and forest beyond; no people, modern tools or invented sandalwood labels.

scenes.title: Stones from Seilan
scenes.caption: He wrote that Seilan, Sri Lanka, produced the finest rubies in the world, and that its king owned one a palm long, flawless and red as fire. Kublai, he said, had offered a city for it and been refused.
scenes.prompt: Close view merchant's small cloth tray of natural corundum ruby and sapphire pebbles and rough crystals, simple metal balance nearby, Sri Lankan shaded veranda, no giant fully faceted modern gems.

composition.view: Close view merchant's small cloth tray of natural corundum ruby and sapphire pebbles and rough crystals, simple metal balance nearby, Sri Lankan shaded veranda, no giant fully faceted modern gems.

scenes.title: The pearl fishery
scenes.caption: In Maabar, on the Gulf of Mannar, he described pearl divers going down from boats into four to twelve fathoms of water. They paid a tenth to the king and a share to the Brahmins who charmed the sharks so they would not attack.

scenes.title: Sorting the catch
scenes.caption: He wrote that the king of Maabar wore a necklace of 104 large pearls and rubies, one for each prayer he said every day. The king allowed no large pearls to leave his kingdom.

scenes.title: Rounding the southern cape
scenes.caption: At Comari, Cape Comorin, he saw the Pole Star again for the first time since Java, just above the horizon. From here the ships turned north up the Malabar coast.
scenes.prompt: Distant sternward sea view low rocky Kanyakumari cape where ocean currents meet, one small sailboat near coast, natural rock islets, no modern Vivekananda memorial or giant statue.

composition.view: Distant sternward sea view low rocky Kanyakumari cape where ocean currents meet, one small sailboat near coast, natural rock islets, no modern Vivekananda memorial or giant statue.

scenes.title: Pepper at Quilon
scenes.caption: At Coilum, now Kollam, he described pepper gathered in May, June and July from vines planted and watered like crops. He also noted brazilwood and the best indigo, made from a herb soaked in water and dried in the sun.

scenes.title: Landfall in Persia
scenes.caption: After eighteen months at sea the fleet reached Hormuz. Of some six hundred people who had sailed, he wrote, only eighteen survived, among them the princess and one of the three envoys.
scenes.prompt: Medium shore-level scene tired Marco around39 steps from small boat onto mainland Hormuz landing while companions unload light luggage, older weathered features, no celebratory crowd or corpses, no laterislandfort.

composition.view: Medium shore-level scene tired Marco around39 steps from small boat onto mainland Hormuz landing while companions unload light luggage, older weathered features, no celebratory crowd or corpses, no laterislandfort.

scenes.title: Tablets for the road west
scenes.caption: Arghun had died, so the princess was married to his son Ghazan. The new Ilkhan Gaykhatu gave the Polos four golden tablets of authority, and while they were in Persia news came that Kublai himself had died.

scenes.title: Reduced baggage at Trebizond
scenes.caption: At Trebizond, on the Black Sea, the Polos were robbed of part of their goods. Fifteen years later, Maffeo's will still recorded the property taken from them in the empire of Trebizond.
scenes.prompt: Quiet harbor warehouse scene Marco40 and older companion examine opened half-empty cloth sacks beside securely stacked surviving baggage, Black Sea harbor doorway, no violent robbery reenactment.

composition.view: Quiet harbor warehouse scene Marco40 and older companion examine opened half-empty cloth sacks beside securely stacked surviving baggage, Black Sea harbor doorway, no violent robbery reenactment.

scenes.title: Through the Bosporus
scenes.caption: From Trebizond they sailed along the Black Sea to Constantinople, where the Venetians had their own quarter. The book says almost nothing about this last stage; Marco was nearly home.
scenes.prompt: View from merchant ship over low gunwale toward1295 Constantinople sea walls and Byzantine domes on hill, Hagia Sophia without minarets, no Ottoman skyline or modern suspension bridges.

composition.view: View from merchant ship over low gunwale toward1295 Constantinople sea walls and Byzantine domes on hill, Hagia Sophia without minarets, no Ottoman skyline or modern suspension bridges.

scenes.title: The narrow channel at Negroponte
scenes.caption: On the way home they called at Negroponte, the Venetian port on Euboea, beside the narrow Euripus strait. From here Venetian ships followed the coasts of Greece and Dalmatia up to Venice.
scenes.prompt: Low shore view narrow Euripus channel and medieval Euboea waterfront with simple stone tower and small boats, distant modest crossing if visible, no Ottoman mosque or modern cable bridge.

composition.view: Low shore view narrow Euripus channel and medieval Euboea waterfront with simple stone tower and small boats, distant modest crossing if visible, no Ottoman mosque or modern cable bridge.

scenes.title: Venice after twenty-four years
scenes.caption: They reached Venice in 1295, twenty-four years after leaving; Marco was about forty-one. A story first printed in 1559 says even their relatives did not know them until they slit open their old coats and jewels spilled out.
scenes.prompt: Side-rear view weathered Marco41 with short dark beard flecked grey and travel cloak at Venetian waterside doorway, elderly father and uncle behind, modest medieval brick and timber buildings, no Renaissance palaces.

composition.view: Side-rear view weathered Marco41 with short dark beard flecked grey and travel cloak at Venetian waterside doorway, elderly father and uncle behind, modest medieval brick and timber buildings, no Renaissance palaces.

evidence.passage: Prologue; Ramusio (1559) for the homecoming story.

scenes.title: What came home
scenes.caption: The book says they came home rich, and Venetian documents show Marco as a prosperous merchant for the rest of his life. In his will of 1324 he freed his servant Peter, 'of the Tartar race'.

scenes.title: The journey becomes a book
scenes.caption: Captured by the Genoese, perhaps at the battle of Curzola in 1298, he dictated his travels in prison to a fellow captive, the romance writer Rustichello of Pisa. On his deathbed, urged to take back its marvels, he is said to have replied that he had not told half of what he saw.
